steps.purpose: Flag and remove unreadable, tiny, strip-shaped and blank images; the pass also hashes every image for the duplicate audit.
Remove empty and very short captions; flag repeated, boilerplate and panel-referencing ones.
Screen pretrained encoders on held-out pairs (label-free) and extract image and caption features.
Frequency audit of 'concepts': imbalance, long tail and how many labels have the support to be judged.
Frequency audit of 'concepts_manual': imbalance, long tail and how many labels have the support to be judged.
Find near-duplicate images (confirmed hashes, calibrated embedding cosine); clusters crossing splits or articles are leakage.
Agreement of 'concepts' with 'concepts_manual' per shared label: an estimate of label noise.
Flag labels their caption does not support or negates, and captions naming a label the sample lacks.
Flag image-caption pairs that match worse than random partners (noisy or mismatched captions), with articles kept together in cross-fitting.
Score how atypical every image is under a cross-fitted density model, as a quality signal next to the QC flags.
Predict 'concepts' from image features with article- and duplicate-grouped folds, a single test evaluation, BH control and the configured reliability rule.
Predict the 18 manually curated concepts from image features under the same leakage-safe design, to check reliability verdicts against cleaner labels.
A two-dimensional map of the image features for the report.

decisions.chosen: predict_targets on multilabel.concepts_manual with article groups and duplicate clusters
decisions.rationale: The objective reading lists concepts_manual as the reference for predictive_modelling. On its 18 shared labels, 'concepts' has precision 0.937 (recall 1.0). That label noise could push a concept's lower DeLong bound below 0.8. 17 of the 18 manual labels can be assessed. The step costs about 67 s against 10,800 s.

68% of samples share an article (1.77 per article). Captions repeat across splits too: 27.6% of the duplicate captions cross the split. If article-mates are not kept together, cross-fitted alignment and the random-partner baseline are inflated.

The results answer the objective. On the noisy 'concepts' labels, 176 of the 214 assessable concepts are reliably predictable (test median AUROC 0.940, CV 0.943). All 17 assessable manual concepts are reliable (AUROC 0.996). Leakage gaps are negligible (≤0.0005), so the grouped and duplicate-aware design holds.
